name: Catherine Wassef
identity: Pediatric Neurosurgeon, Nemours Children's Health, Wilmington, DE (Nemours Children's Hospital, Delaware).
bio: Wassef is a fellowship-trained pediatric neurosurgeon who joined Nemours' Delaware division as an early-career attending. Her self-described clinical focus is epilepsy surgery and minimally invasive approaches to brain surgery, which she pursued specifically through her pediatric neurosurgery fellowship at Children's Hospital Colorado (a high-volume epilepsy/ablation center). As a brand-new attending her independent case mix is not yet reflected in claims data, but her stated orientation points toward the intractable-epilepsy and lesional case types most amenable to stereotactic laser ablation.

name: Joseph Piatt
identity: Chief, Division of Neurosurgery (Pediatric Neurosurgery), Nemours Children's Health, Wilmington, DE; Professor of Neurological Surgery & Pediatrics, Sidney Kimmel Medical College, Thomas Jefferson University.
bio: Piatt is a senior, academically prominent pediatric neurosurgeon who has led the Nemours (A.I. duPont) division in Wilmington since 2010 after prior chief roles at St. Christopher's Hospital for Children (Philadelphia) and OHSU. His clinical practice centers on hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation/syringomyelia, spinal dysraphism, craniosynostosis, pediatric craniospinal trauma, and primary brain tumors. His scholarly output is dominated by epidemiology and outcomes research (hydrocephalus, trauma triage, quality improvement) rather than device-driven or ablation surgery. Claims show a modest epilepsy footprint (SEEG and epilepsy-related craniotomy), consistent with a general pediatric practice rather than a dedicated laser-ablation program.
training: University of Pennsylvania (MD) · Neurosurgery residency, Duke University · Pediatric neurosurgery fellowship, The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto (while on active U.S. Army duty) · Pedigree note: Swarthmore College undergrad; Penn/Duke/SickKids lineage; long-tenured division chief and prolific academic (FAANS).
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Cohort flag is 'LITT-Naïve Craniotomy Surgeon.' His publication record and clinical bio show open/traditional pediatric neurosurgery (hydrocephalus, trauma, dysraphism, craniosynostosis) with no laser-ablation authorship or program involvement located.
wheelhouse: Senior academic generalist pediatric neurosurgeon / epidemiology & outcomes researcher; open-surgery and hydrocephalus focus
kol_note: Genuine academic KOL — named professor at Sidney Kimmel/Jefferson, long-standing division chief, and a prolific, frequently cited author on pediatric neurosurgical epidemiology, hydrocephalus outcomes, and quality improvement. KOL influence is in health-services/epidemiology, not in ablation technology.
